ideas.title: Daily-EMA recovery swing, no trigger on the session's first bar
ideas.hypothesis: When the first 15-minute bar of the session closes back above the prior day's daily EMA, the 'reclaim' is usually an overnight gap through the level rather than buyers winning it back during the day, so it carries none of the setup's information and a stop under that bar's lows is hit by ordinary opening noise. Taking the same daily-EMA reclaim only once the session has traded should keep the real reclaims and drop the gap-throughs. The trader's own journal points the same way independently: their entries from 09:30 to 09:45 lost money while 09:45 to 10:00 was their best window.
ideas.change: The entry window only: fills allowed from 10:00 instead of any time, which removes triggers on the first 15-minute bar (09:30-09:45) of each session. Trigger level (daily EMA), arming, breakout confirmation, stop, 2R target and two-session hold are unchanged.

answer.lessons: Nothing has passed yet. The two one-minute intraday patterns pick entries a little better than random, but their stops are so tight that trading costs eat more than the edge, so more tweaks to targets or holds on one-minute bars are not worth sending. The recovery swing is the only pattern that makes money before costs, and triggering it on the daily EMA instead of the 15-minute EMA was the best result so far (about +0.15R a trade, t near 1.9), still short of the bar. In both recovery-swing versions, trades triggered on the very first 15-minute bar of the day are clearly the worst slice, and it is much worse in the daily-EMA version, so removing them is the most mechanical fix left; the same cut did not rescue the weaker 15-minute-EMA version. The confirmation bar is now t >= 2.61 and rises with each candidate that reaches it, so only ideas with a mechanical reason to work should be sent.
wanted: A conditional time stop: exit after N minutes (e.g. 60) only if the trade has not reached a set progress level such as +0.5R, so trades that are working keep their target and multi-session hold while stalled ones are cut. A plain max_minutes cap would also cut the winners, and the swing family's end-of-session exits are its best trades.
An intraday family built on 5- or 15-minute bars with wider stops, so a same-day 60-minute hold can be tested without one-minute trading costs swamping the signal.

A feature for the opening gap measured against the reclaim level (did the open already sit above the daily EMA), to separate gap-throughs from true intraday reclaims directly instead of by time of day.
